methodology.typedIdentityRule: Legal tracks, explicit track units, compiled pathways, effective route-contract service branches, effective route-contract failure dispositions, and all current research-track decision routes are preserved as separate typed evidence entities. The two batch-B unattached decisions retain their own subtype. Crosswalk edges and exact current-decision representation joins relate source identities and never license fuzzy deduplication.
methodology.canonicalObligationRule: Classification is over terminal obligations once: mapped non-unit track/runtime edges, unmapped non-unit tracks, explicit units in place of their abstract parents, runtime-only pathways, exact contract service branches, failure dispositions, current-decision route stages, and current-decision correction or enforcement branches. A runtime-to-unit-parent edge expands to the units without guessing a unit/pathway assignment. Exact AK ak-set-aside and OH oh-ls-5 research representations map to their existing obligations. Shared-form-only edges without shared statutory citations and held route-presentation conflations are retained as evidence but rejected as canonicalization authority.
methodology.contractPrecedence: Last file wins in the runtime import order: src/lib/legal-authority/routes/p0.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/mississippi.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/route-splits.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/single-routes.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/national-report-2026-08-28.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/national-report-batch-b.json -> src/lib/legal-authority/routes/national-report-batch-c.json
methodology.paidSubsetRule: The 260 intended-paid launch/factory rows are evidence joins only and never define or filter this universe.

sourceRecord.provenBy: LD-GA-01 / GA-35-3-37-42-8-62.1-THREE-MECHANISM-MAP. The contract names § 42-8-62.1, effectiveFrom 2026-07-01, mechanism "First-offender restriction and sealing under the July 1, 2026 amendments", packetFamily "Georgia First-Offender Restriction and Sealing Petition under § 42-8-62.1", packetComponents "Petition or motion under § 42-8-62.1" and "First-offender discharge documentation". Its own exclusions push the other mechanisms away by name: "Separate post-July 1, 2013 nonconviction, pardoned-felony, and first-offender mechanisms". The contract is specific, coherent and self-consistent.
sourceRecord.whatIsConflated: The compiled pathway text, not the contract. src/lib/rcap-engine/compiled/profiles/GA-georgia.json carries this route's summary and ruleClauses straight from corpus-unit:29 (pathways:68-115), which is the whole Georgia restriction-and-sealing chapter. Its clauses describe § 35-3-37(h) non-conviction restriction, § 35-3-37(j.1) automatic restriction, § 35-3-37(j)(4) SB 288 misdemeanor restriction, § 35-3-37(j)(7) pardoned-felony restriction, § 35-3-37(m) clerk-file sealing, and § 42-8-66 retroactive First Offender treatment. Five of those six have their own separate Georgia routes. Section 42-8-62.1 — the statute the contract is about — appears in none of the route's own clauses.
sourceRecord.whyItIsHeld: A participant on this route can be shown a summary about GCIC restriction under § 35-3-37 while the packet family and components prepare a petition under § 42-8-62.1. The canonical resolver already treats this route as a sellable participant packet: serviceDisposition participant_packet, paymentAuthority packet_checkout, no open delivery gates, delivery.paymentAllowed true. Today the evaluator returns guidance_only for an unrelated reason — ga.lawrence_hold_guidance_only — so nothing sells. That hold is not about this conflict and could be lifted without anyone noticing this one. This row makes the hold specific to the defect.
sourceRecord.notAnAlias: This is also the answer to whether the new § 42-8-66 route is a rename of this one. It is not. The texts overlap because this route's text is a chapter dump that happens to mention § 42-8-66; the contracts do not overlap at all, and LD-GA-01 excludes the § 42-8-66 mechanism by name.

An excluded conviction inside an eligible group is omitted or severed rather than carried. The reply period after an opposition is thirty days under subsection (g)(3), not the ten days the SCA-C900 instruction sheet prints against subsection (e).

unattachedDecisionFindings.reportSaysNow: Not yet legally operative. The amending provisions take effect 2027-01-01. As of 2026-08-28 this participant-request route does not exist in law.
unattachedDecisionFindings.reportSaysLater: The temporary request condition is repealed 2028-01-01, after which the statutory nondisclosure becomes automatic for qualifying records. So the route is a participant request for one year and then stops being a request at all.
unattachedDecisionFindings.mechanismWhenItArrives: An agency request, not a court petition. Default destination the Department of Public Safety central repository, with additional agency-specific requests where another criminal justice agency holds and releases the record.

unattachedDecisionFindings.reportSaysNow: Operative. The participant challenges the record through the Department of Public Safety or the agency responsible for the disputed data, using the published Request to Correct Criminal Justice Information form.
unattachedDecisionFindings.mechanismWhenItArrives: An agency application. The challenge identifies the precise entry, why it is inaccurate or incomplete, the correct disposition or data, the originating agency and case, certified disposition, identity documents and fingerprints where required, and the correction requested.
